newsitem.title: UK: Personal Investment Authority appoints ombudsman.
newsitem.headline: Personal Investment Authority appoints ombudsman.

text.p: The UK's Personal Investment Authority (PIA) said on Monday it had appointed Anthony Holland as its principal ombudsman to succeed Stephen Edell, the watchdog's first ombudsman.

"Stephen Edell has set this ombudsman scheme on a firm foundation. Anthony Holland...can continue to provide impartial direction to the resolution of disputes and ensure that all complaints referred to him are properly considered," the PIA council chairman Baroness Turner of Camden said in a statement.
The PIA is one of the UK's so-called self-regulatory organisations, charged with regulating companies in the personal investments market.
Holland, 58, is a solicitor and a past president of the Law Society. Edell has held the post of ombudsman since July 1994 but retires in June 1997.
